items.title: Charles McPherson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2024 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I was reading something about Beethoven, like a kind of biographical thing.

ctx.x: Yeah. I was involved in an aesthetic education program for some years and you’re making me think of how we used to connect the different art forms and that observing an abstract painting or watching a dance performance — especially a modern dance performance — and being able to make some cognitive sense about it applies certainly to your playing as well.

Yeah I think it applies to everything. So what I mean by that is — I was reading something about Beethoven, like a kind of biographical thing. And he made a statement that was curious. And he said, “If you know the secret of correspondence you can do anything.” And I think I understood what that meant, and that’s kind of what Barry meant. And I see what it means now. And basically when you say looking at dance, looking at art, if you’re able to look at anything and see how it corresponds to any other

thing, no matter what the construct is, no matter what the medium through which a particular behavior is being — it doesn’t make any difference. You see the — you see the correspondence between the two supposedly different constructs. But the behavior — you can see it. So then you become — you understand the DNA of metaphor and the DNA of analogy — analogists. You can see the thing. And the only difference is the mediums through which particular things are being expressed, but it’s still being expressed by human…
